blocks.markdown: **MONDAY  |  From Console to Window: Swing and Safe Startup**

A graphical user interface (GUI) lets a person use windows and controls with a keyboard or mouse. Swing is Java’s built-in toolkit for these controls. AWT (Abstract Window Toolkit) supplies older controls, window support, events, and layout tools; Swing builds on AWT [NTU].
The terminal window is the service counter. A label is the sign above it. The event dispatch thread is the clerk who changes signs and handles requests, one short job at a time.
The **event dispatch thread (EDT)** creates and updates the interface and handles its actions. invokeLater queues a job there [NTU] [NUS].

blocks.markdown: **TUESDAY  |  A Click Has a Job: Buttons, Text Fields, and Listeners**

An event is a report that something happened, such as a click. An ActionListener is an object whose actionPerformed method responds to that report. Register it with addActionListener; otherwise the button has no action [HWS] [MIT].
A button is the bell at a sari-sari store. Ringing it is the event; the listener is the shopkeeper’s agreed response. A bell with no response plan makes noise but serves nobody.

blocks.markdown: **THURSDAY  |  Keep the Window Responsive: Background Work and Safe Updates**

A responsive interface continues to handle actions while work is in progress. A background thread does the slow job. The event dispatch thread (EDT), introduced Monday, handles interface actions and updates. SwingUtilities.invokeLater queues an update on the EDT [NTU] [NUS].
The clerk asks a helper to check a loading bay. The clerk can still answer other customers. The helper returns a report; only the clerk changes the counter sign.

blocks.markdown: **Main.java**
**ReadyTask.java**
**What happens and why**
The inner listener captures status and check: it keeps access to those local variables. Java 8 allows this because they are not reassigned. The final outcome value also cannot be reassigned.
The worker uses Week 16 Runnable and start(). It sleeps to simulate a slow check, then queues a Runnable on the EDT to update the sign and restore the button.
Interruption is a stop request. Restore its flag and report the interruption. Never make the EDT wait by calling join, await, or sleep in a listener.
**Observed console result**
No display: GUI not opened.

**School-computer test:** click Check ready. Expect Checking... and a disabled button, followed by Ready: NXA 123 and an enabled button. While waiting, quote BUS 789 at 4 km; expect P25.00 without waiting for readiness. Record the actual behavior.

**Check yourself.** while Check ready is running, try Quote fare. The fare action should still work; the ready button should be disabled until the update. Do not call join, await, or sleep in the listener. Record whether your school computer passes this test.
Sources [1 NTU] [2 HWS] [3 MIT] [4 CMU] [5 NUS] . Key validated facts: Workers can queue interface updates using invokeLater [NTU] [NUS]; the window remains active after main ends [HWS].

blocks.markdown: Compiler wording above was produced with JDK 21 using Java 8 compatibility checks; the API-compatible programs use only Java 8 features. Compiler line numbers and newer-JDK warnings may differ. Each runtime message was produced by an actual run. The HeadlessException came from a separate unguarded display probe.

**Keep the model:** Vehicle is abstract; Jeepney, Tricycle, and Bus supply their own fare and capacity. FareService calls quoteFare rather than copying formulas. VehicleNotFoundException and OverloadException are checked; InvalidDistanceException is unchecked. Boarding is not used in the fare action. Locale.ROOT fixes decimal formatting independently of computer language.
**When no error message appears**

rows: Look behind other windows; check setVisible(true). A display-server connection error is an environment problem, not a fare rule.
Check addActionListener and method spelling. Recompile after saving.
Find sleep, join, await, or slow file work inside a listener; move the job to a background thread.
Text or controls are hard to read
Resize on the school display. Keep clear labels. Report clipping instead of claiming an unobserved appearance is correct.

blocks.markdown: **What was actually verified**

All complete printed programs compiled with javac --release 8 and ran. GUI launchers reported “No display: GUI not opened.” FareCheck and ThemeCheck produced the printed console results. Separate headless component checks exercised listener actions, invalid-input recovery, background completion/interruption, and an EDT action while the worker was waiting. Window appearance, physical mouse clicks, keyboard navigation, resizing, and closing could not be observed: the display server was unreachable and no virtual display was installed.
